posts.design_recipe:
**Reusable Carousel Template (4 slides) — EHN Hormonal/Physiological Education Format**

**Canvas:** Carousel, 4 slides, 1080px square (Instagram/Facebook standard).

**Background:** Warm cream or soft neutral (e.g., #F5F3F0, #FAF9F7, or a muted warm grey-taupe) — harmonises with EHN green #39B54A, never pure white or black.

**Colour Anchor:** EHN green #39B54A appears in:
- Headline accent word (italic, same size as headline, integrated into Satoshi Bold typography).
- Icon/illustration elements (top-right or integrated into chart).
- Logo/brand close line at slide bottom.
- Chart/graph line (solid green) or border highlight (thin green stroke).

**Secondary Palette:** Sage grey, muted taupe, soft cool grey-blue, or warm charcoal — chosen to harmonise with green, never to clash (no purples, bright pinks, neons, or strong reds).

**Typography:**
- Headline: Satoshi Bold (700), ~95px visual scale (Slide 1 chart hook), ~80px (Slides 2–4 text slides). ONE meaningful word in green #39B54A italic, integrated into the line.
- Supporting line (Slide 1): Satoshi Medium, ~50px visual scale.
- Body copy (Slides 2–4): Satoshi Medium (500), ~50px visual weight (short, punchy lines; NEVER compress below legible scale).
- Attribution / small text: Satoshi Medium, ~36px visual equivalent, charcoal.
- Brand line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" (Satoshi Medium), green #39B54A, bottom of every slide.

**Slide 1 (Hook/Chart Slide) Layout:**
- Headline top-left or centre (Satoshi Bold, ~95px): "[Keyword] *[green-accented word]*".
- Supporting line directly below (Satoshi Medium, ~50px): "[Brief physiological setup or question]".
- Centre: white card (soft rounded corners, 12–16px radius; subtle shadow for depth) containing a **chart/graph** (dual-line or multi-element diagram).
  - X-axis: lifecycle stages or time progression.
  - Y-axis: relative concentration or scale (no busy numbers; visual only).
  - Primary line: solid EHN green #39B54A.
  - Secondary line(s): soft sage, taupe, or muted grey — dotted or dashed for contrast.
  - Highlight zone (e.g., perimenopause): subtle box with thin green #39B54A border, no fill (respects whitespace).
- Bottom of card: attribution line (Satoshi Medium, charcoal, small).
- Bottom of slide: brand line "Elemental Health & Nutrition" (green #39B54A).

**Slides 2–4 (Educational Text Slides) Layout:**
- Headline top-centre or left (Satoshi Bold, ~80px): "[Topic description] *[green-accented word]*".
- Body copy centre-left (Satoshi Medium, ~50px visual weight): short, punchy sentences (2–3 lines max). SHORTEN COPY rather than compress font.
- Icon/illustration top-right or integrated (simple, line-drawn or minimalist; green #39B54A or soft secondary colour; 80–120px scale).
- Ample whitespace around text and icon (matches winner's clean, spacious layout).
- Bottom: brand line "Elemental Health & Nutrition" (green #39B54A).

**Overall Feel:** Clinical-but-warm, educational infographic style. Whitespace-heavy, never cluttered. Colour hierarchy: green anchors, secondary tones support, charcoal text reads. Australian natural palette (sage, cream, charcoal) — grounded, not trendy. Every slide feels part of one coherent carousel; the Slide 1 chart sets the premise, Slides 2–4 expand on mechanisms.

**Legibility Lock:** All on-slide text ≥36px visual hierarchy; body copy ≥50px visual weight. No text compressed to sub-36px. Headline ~95px (Slide 1), ~80px (Slides 2–4). If copy runs long, edit/shorten the message — never shrink the font.

posts.caption:
Many women assume oestrogen is the main event at perimenopause, but progesterone actually drops first—and it's a big deal. 💚

This anti-inflammatory, calming hormone does serious work. When it declines early in the perimenopausal window, inflammation rises, anxiety can climb, and histamine regulation loosens. That's why some women experience hot flushes, joint discomfort, and sleep disruption well before their periods become irregular.

Understanding *why* symptoms show up—not just managing the symptoms—changes how we approach this life stage. If this sounds like your journey, there's a lot we can do to support hormonal rhythm through functional medicine and lifestyle.

Ready to understand what's happening? Book a consultation with us and let's map your hormonal story.

#perimenopause #hormonehealth #progesterone #functionalhealth #womenswellness #Adelaide

posts.caption:
Anxiety often shows up with a second shadow: sleep disruption. And the link is physiological, not just "in your head."

When cortisol runs high, your nervous system stays wired come evening — tough to wind down, tougher to stay asleep. Poor sleep then amplifies emotional reactivity the next day, and the cycle feeds itself.

In functional medicine, we look at both layers: the neurochemical patterns that keep you awake, and the sleep quality that allows your nervous system to reset. Supporting one usually settles the other.

If anxiety and sleep troubles feel linked for you, it's worth exploring the root — not just managing the symptom.

Ready to understand what's driving yours? We're here to help.

#AuxietyAndSleep #FunctionalHealth #NervousSystemHealth #SleepMatters #MentalWellness

Fasting isn't just about skipping breakfast—it's a metabolic reset. When you give your digestive system a genuine rest, your cells shift into repair mode (a process called autophagy), insulin sensitivity improves, and inflammation often drops. Ready to explore whether fasting is right for you? Let's chat about what sustainable, evidence-based nutrition looks like for you.

posts.caption:
There's real neuroscience behind why dimming the lights before bed changes everything. When you shower or prepare for sleep in low light—especially warm, amber-toned light like candlelight—you're signalling to your nervous system that it's safe to unwind. Your pupils dilate, your cortisol drops, and melatonin begins its evening climb. We recommend this simple ritual to patients managing nervous-system overload, poor sleep, or that constant "wired but tired" feeling. No fancy gadgets, no screens—just you, warm light, and permission to slow down. Try it for a week and notice what shifts. If sleep remains elusive, that's worth exploring together—sometimes there's more to the story.

Book an appointment to discuss your sleep patterns with our team.
